messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] SLO breach detected for /v1/stream — p99 latency 7.4s (SLO 2s). Paging @ryan_oncall. Severity: seve3. Runbook: /runbooks/streaming-tail.

sara_ops: paging in. seeing sustained p95/p99 drift and intermittent chunk gaps on SSE consumers. proxy shows bursts of backpressure + client-side resets. @ryan_oncall you on? :raised_hand:

ryan_oncall: oncall here. investigating. when did this start showing up? any customer correlation?

mike_prod: started ~08:12 UTC. correlates with a sudden spike of long prompts from a single customer. Logs show repeated 'write buffer full' on proxy and WS stall metrics climbing. snippet of recent logs:
```
[08:14:23] proxy: write backlog=3240 bytes -> client=192.168.10.22
[08:14:24] runtime: kv-cache miss, fallback path exec_time=210ms
[08:14:25] sse: chunk_sent id=0x7f but client_ack delayed > 2s
[08:14:26] proxy: upstream 504 write timeout for conn_id=1023
```

linda_support: CS reporting a premium customer seeing partial streams and timeouts; impacted sessions ~120 (~5% of live streams). They have some older SDK clients. Customer on a call now.

ryan_oncall: immediate mitigations proposal (quick and reversible):
1) disable proxy buffering for /v1/stream (nginx proxy_buffering off) to reduce head-of-line stalls
2) reduce runtime max_chunk_size to 8KB to increase frequency of flushes
3) temporarily route new streaming requests to a lower-latency fallback model (e.g., redwood-mini-v1) to relieve token generation pressure
4) trigger scale-up of streaming pool by +2 GPUs if autoscaler won't catch up
I'll apply 1+2 now.

sara_ops: applying nginx toggle for streaming location: `kubectl exec -n infra proxy-84 -- sed -i '/location \/v1\/stream/,/}/s/proxy_buffering on;/proxy_buffering off;/' /etc/nginx/nginx.conf && nginx -s reload` — changes pushed.

devex-faith: routing patch applied to gateway: 
```
PATCH /config/routes
{ "route": "/v1/stream", "fallback_model": "redwood-mini-v1", "reason": "mitigation-1998765432" }
```
applied and returning 200.

mike_prod: scaling request submitted to dedicated pool (req id 0x7f3). if autoscaler takes >3m we'll consider draining longest requests.

incident-bot: bridge created: https://internal/bridges/1998765432 — pinned to channel.

linda_support: quick customer update: after toggles the customer reports fewer partial responses, still 2–3 reconnects for older SDK clients; CS pushing recommended client patch to reduce read buffer.

ryan_oncall: monitoring metrics now. p95 dropped from ~2.1s -> ~1.6s; p99 dropped from 7.4s -> ~3.0s after mitigations. Proxy 504s decreasing. Scaling still in progress. Will keep bridge open and monitor for 30m.

sara_ops: handoff notes for next shift: - proxy_buffering off is temporary; revert when stable - collect payload samples from impacted sessions and match to customer ids (mike_prod) - add per-customer tail-load alert to prevent one tenant from saturating streaming pool - consider a per-client circuit breaker and token-generation rate limiter - investigate KV cache behavior under long prompts

ryan_oncall: agreed. Logging actions: saved debug logs and metrics snapshot -> /mnt/incident/1998765432/artifacts.tar.gz. I'll notify oncall-next for handoff at 09:00 UTC and keep this thread for postmortem.

linda_support: customer summary drafted and sent; offering best-effort credits and guidance for SDK patch. :pray:

mike_prod: saved relevant traces and instance metrics. also captured some websocket-level pcap for one impacted session.

incident-bot: severity downgraded to seve2 at 08:46 UTC; paging stopped.

ryan_oncall: immediate mitigation successful enough to stop the pager. Bridge remains open for 30m and then we'll close and create a follow-up postmortem ticket (PM-1998765432). Handoff complete.
